notes: ACCESS: Tier 1 (direct curl/WebFetch HTTP) failed with a genuine block on this Akamai-fronted host — curl connected but the TLS session stalled through repeated schannel renegotiations and timed out with 0 bytes (exit 56); WebFetch also timed out on both robots.txt and the homepage. Escalated per the hard-block rule to Claude-in-Chrome (no separate Playwright/CDP tool is available in this environment) — this succeeded and gave full DOM/network access, so this is a genuine tier-2/3 use, not a shortcut. Checked robots.txt first (fetched in-browser since curl/WebFetch couldn't reach it): 'User-agent: *' only, no Claude-specific disallow (no anthropic-ai/ClaudeBot/Claude-Web/Claude-User/Claude-SearchBot entries) — proceeded. Note robots.txt disallows generic bot crawling of '*/ar-ae*' and several specific slugs (decoded from an apparent 'id'->'code' text-mangling artifact in the raw file, e.g. 'holcodeay-tables-18780' = 'holiday-tables-18780', 'holcodeays-gifts-18634' = 'holidays-gifts-18634', 'kcodes' = 'kids'); none of these are Claude-specific and none block the pages actually used below. DISCOVERY: top nav 'Gifts' link goes to the site's single holiday/occasion hub at /en-ae/c/holidays-gifts-18634 ('Holiday Gifts', breadcrumb 'Home > Holidays & Gifts'). Its carousel + left-rail CATEGORY facet (which only lists facet values with >0 matching products) exposed exactly 5 sub-nodes: Gift Ideas (1297), View All Gifts (726), Mother's Day (166), Easter (135), Fathers Day (41) — plus a Christmas tile that is NOT in the facet list (0 current matches). Cross-checked against the site's own sitemap (Category + CategoryLanding XML sitemaps, fetched and grepped): confirms /holidays-gifts-18634/christmas-13, /holidays-gifts-18634/easter and /holidays-gifts-18634/mothers-day exist as real indexed category-landing nodes; fathers-day resolves live (41 items, matches facet) even though not separately listed in the sampled sitemap files. INCLUDED: Christmas, Easter, Mother's Day, Father's Day — each is a genuine standalone PLP (own URL, own SEO copy/description, in main nav and/or sitemap) that the site itself frames as one of its named holiday/celebration occasions (breadcrumb 'Holidays & Gifts > <name>'), matching the 'celebration/seasonal event' test in the boundary rules. EXCLUDED 'Gift Ideas' and 'View All Gifts' — generic all-occasion gift buckets, not tied to any specific holiday, and the parent 'Holidays & Gifts' hub itself is not given its own row since it mixes multiple unrelated holidays (not a single-holiday grouping with subset children, so it doesn't fit the is_group pattern; treated like an ordinary nav section, not a holiday). CHRISTMAS = 0: the Christmas PLP (https://www.crateandbarrel.me/en-ae/c/holidays-gifts-18634/christmas-13) renders full SEO/marketing copy about Christmas trees, stockings, ornaments etc. but no product grid, no item-count header, and no filter sidebar — it is simply absent from the sibling CATEGORY facet counts on the parent hub page (which lists every category with >=1 match). Confirmed via read_network_requests that no product/search API call fired for that page load. Also ran the on-site search for 'christmas' — 0 results sitewide, consistent with the category being genuinely out of stock/off-season (checked 2026-09-04) rather than a broken or missing page. Recorded as qty 0 (a real, corroborated displayed absence), not null/manual-review, given the multiple independent confirming signals. WESTERN vs EID/RAMADAN CHECK (per task instructions): searched on-site search for 'eid' and 'ramadan' — 0 results for both, no matching category or product. No Halloween, Diwali, Valentine's Day, Thanksgiving, New Year, Eid or Ramadan node appears anywhere in the main nav (Best Sellers/Inspiration/Furniture/Outdoor/Tabletop & Bar/Kitchen/Bedding & Bath/Rugs/Decor/Lighting/Gifts/Home Office/&Kids), the SALE/New mega-menus, the Holidays & Gifts hub's own facets/carousel, or the Category/CategoryLanding sitemap XML files (grepped full sitemap text for all of: christmas, halloween, easter, diwali, valentine, thanksgiving, new-year, eid, ramadan, holiday, mothers-day, fathers-day). Did not check the ar-ae Arabic storefront's own separate navigation beyond confirming it exists in the sitemap index (robots.txt disallows '*/ar-ae*' for generic crawlers and it mirrors the same en-ae commerce platform/taxonomy, so a materially different holiday taxonomy there is unlikely, but this was not independently verified live). No duplicate-link cases found — each of the 4 included rows has a distinct URL and a distinct item count matching its own facet value.
